faq.q: Which barcode format should I use — retail product, shipping carton, or internal inventory?
faq.a: For a retail product scanned at a checkout, use EAN-13 (used in India and most of the world) or UPC-A (North America). For a shipping or logistics carton, use ITF-14. For your own internal inventory, assets or IDs — where no public standard is required — use CODE128 (compact, handles letters and digits) or CODE39. The tool offers all of these plus EAN-8, UPC-E, ITF, MSI, Codabar and pharmacode.

faq.q: What is the check digit, and can I leave it off?
faq.a: EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A and ITF-14 end in a check digit that is calculated from the other digits using the GS1 modulo-10 formula, so a scanner can detect a misread. You can type the number with OR without it: enter 12 digits for EAN-13 and the tool appends the check digit and shows it; enter all 13 and it verifies the last one. If your check digit is wrong, the tool tells you the exact digit it expected (for example, for 590123412345 it expects 7, giving 5901234123457) instead of just saying 'invalid'.

faq.q: I printed a barcode and it will not scan — why?
faq.a: The three usual causes are the quiet zone, contrast and size. The quiet zone is the blank margin on each side; set the Margin option high enough (a common mistake is cropping it off). Contrast must be high — dark bars on a light background; the tool warns you if contrast is too low or if your bars are lighter than the background, because most scanners cannot read light-on-dark. Finally, bars printed too small or on a low-resolution printer blur together: export the PNG at 4× or 6× scale, or use the SVG for sharp printing at any size.

faq.q: Can I generate a real retail barcode for selling a product?
faq.a: This tool only draws the bars for whatever number you type — it does not assign you a number. Real EAN-13 and UPC-A numbers for products sold in shops must be licensed from GS1 (GS1 India for Indian sellers); they issue the company prefix that makes your product number globally unique. Use this tool to render a number you already own, to prototype labels, or for internal CODE128/CODE39 codes where no license is needed.
